lesson.intro: A noun is a naming word. It names a [[person]], an [[animal]], a [[place]] or a [[thing]].
points: People: teacher, doctor, baby, my mother
Proper nouns are special names of people, places, days and months. They always begin with a capital letter: [[Siti]], [[Penang]], [[Monday]], [[June]].
Collective nouns name a group: a [[flock]] of birds, a [[herd]] of cows, a [[school]] of fish.
Abstract nouns name things we cannot see or touch, like feelings and ideas: [[happiness]], [[courage]], [[truth]].

examples.note: cat – an animal; sofa – a thing
proper nouns begin with capital letters

examples.text: A [[herd]] of elephants crossed the road.

lesson.tip: Ask yourself: can I put "a", "an" or "the" in front of the word? If yes, it is probably a noun.

questions.prompt: Spot the mistake: tap the word that is wrong.
